**First beta of the 0.4.7 line.** Still a pre-release: not marked Latest, not intended for general use. If you want a stable build, use v0.4.6.

Linux x86_64 only — pre-releases ship the tarball. No `.deb`, `.rpm` or AUR package is built for previews.

The memory work that has dominated the alpha series is complete. This is the build we want flown.

---

## The last of three memory fixes

Issue #227 turned out to be three separate mechanisms wearing one symptom. alpha.3 shipped the first, alpha.4 the second, and this build the third.

**None of them was a leak.** Bytes actually in use stayed flat at 572–725 MB across an eighteen-fold increase in work — everything was being freed. What grew was glibc's *retention* of freed memory, which is why nothing in the code ever looked wrong.

The mechanism, finally: glibc gives each thread a heap arena to avoid lock contention, and returns memory only by trimming the **top** of a heap. Space stranded below a live allocation stays committed for the life of the process. So an arena grows to cover the worst burst it ever saw and never gives that space back, and the total is the sum of every arena's personal high-water mark.

The default ceiling is eight arenas per CPU core — 256 on a 32-core machine. With that many available, every burst can recruit *fresh* arenas that have never seen a peak, so the sum keeps climbing for as long as you fly.

**Rare traffic peaks were being converted into permanent floor, once per arena.**

This build caps the arena count at four. Once each has seen its worst burst, no fresh ones remain and the total stops growing.

### Measured

Same route flown twice, ~11 hours each, compared at matched work:

| | alpha.4 | beta.1 |
|---|---:|---:|
| committed memory at the end | 11,580 MB | **9,687 MB** |
| glibc arena | 6,091 MB | **4,038 MB** |
| swap used | 1,063 MB | **533 MB** |
| arena growth steps after the first six minutes | 18 | **1** |
| textures/second | 3.06 | 3.03 |

The arena settled at 3,916 MB within six minutes and then moved once in eleven hours. Growth after that initial sizing fell from 5,393 MB to 125 MB — a forty-three-fold reduction, and the difference between a slope and a ceiling.

### One thing to know before you test

**Short flights will look worse, and you will be measuring that correctly.**

The cap front-loads the entire arena into the first six minutes, so this build carries about 2 GB more than alpha.4 early on. It draws level near 80,000 textures and only pulls ahead after roughly 98,000 — about nine hours of flying.

If you fly two hours and report higher memory than alpha.4, that is the expected behaviour and not a regression. The win is in the tail.

### What this does not fix

Memory is not flat. Committed still rose from 8,834 MB to 9,687 MB over eleven hours. The arena is bounded now; the remainder moves in memory-mapped allocations, which rise during bursts and come back down. Smaller and far better behaved, but not zero.

The ceiling is also set by our own peak concurrency rather than by any allocator setting — 3,916 MB is the worst simultaneous demand plus about 27% headroom. Prefetching does not currently yield when X-Plane's demand on the mount spikes, and that collision is the peak. Tracked as #246.

All of this is Linux-only; macOS uses a different allocator and has none of it. Tracked as #245.

## Also in this build

`cache.disk_io_profile` has been removed. It never affected I/O concurrency — the limiter built from it was never consulted. Existing configs still load and simply ignore the line; `xearthlayer config upgrade` will tidy it away and write a backup first. Storage detection is unaffected, and `xearthlayer setup` still reports whether your cache lives on NVMe, SSD or a spinning disk.

---

## What to fly

**Six hours or more, and longer is better.** Everything below about 80,000 textures looks the same on every build we have shipped; the differences are all in the tail.

If you hit an out-of-memory kill, the log is what we need:

```
~/.xearthlayer/xearthlayer.log
```

It is overwritten on every launch, so copy it aside before relaunching. Attach it to #227 along with your core count and configured cache sizes.

Two known gaps worth reporting around rather than through:

- Memory is sampled once a minute, so a brief spike between samples leaves no trace. If you see the system balloon and recover, that is real and invisible to us — tell us what you saw and roughly how long it lasted.
- On macOS none of the allocator fields appear in the log at all. That is expected on this build.

If you want to help with the remaining piece, `MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2 xearthlayer run` tests a tighter ceiling than the default we chose. Watch for slower scene loads, which is what that variable can cost.
